feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iterations 0 to 2 show max_error between 0.0604 and 0.0622 m, with every run ending off_track and progress between 0.035 and 0.115. Line loss went from 1 per run (iteration 0, 12 mm footprint with a 0.03 m spread) to 0 from iteration 1 onward (16 mm footprint with a 0.05 m spread). Iteration 2 changed mass, body length and wheel_track (0.12 to 0.10 m), but max_error moved only from 0.0604 to 0.0612. Turn authority and inertia therefore do not appear to be the binding limit, and sensing is no longer losing the line. What I had to compensate for: I kept kp at 2.0 and kd at 0.10 because the lighter, narrower body already raises turn gain, and I left ki at 0 to avoid windup. I did not need any other compensation for your sensor lead. Next race, if max_error stays at about 0.060 m or above and progress stays below 0.2: the forward lead and sensor layout are not curing drift, so try wheel_radius 0.04 m for more ground speed, which lets the robot reach progress above 0.5 and clear the stall limit. If steering_oscillation rises above 0.1 with the lead at y = 0.07 m, return the sensors to y = 0.05 m and keep wheel_track 0.09 m. If max_error falls below 0.055 m on the oval and s-bend but a run still goes off track, widen the spread to +/-0.065 m with 16 mm footprints, to keep the line in view at the larger offset.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above 0.1 with max_error still at or above 0.06 m (iteration 2 gave 0.07 and 0.061 m), return the forward sensor row to y = 0.05 m and keep wheel_track 0.09 m, to test whether the 0.07 m lead is too aggressive.

If max_error stays at or above 0.06 m and progress stays below 0.2 (iterations 0 to 2 all gave max_error 0.060 to 0.062 m and progress 0.035 to 0.115), change wheel_radius to 0.04 m to raise ground speed, since turn authority (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m, iteration 2) did not move max_error.

If max_error falls below 0.055 m on the oval and s-bend but a run still leaves the track, widen the sensor x spread to +/-0.065 m with sensor_size 0.016 m, so the line stays under the sensors at the larger offset (iteration 1 showed line loss was fixed by the 0.05 m spread, and the 0.065 m spread is the next step).
